original_record.question: Three boys play a game a luck in which their respective chances of wining are ½, 1/3 and ¼. What is the probability that one and only of the boys wins the game?
original_record.ai_explanation: P(exactly one wins) = P(A wins, B and C lose) + P(B wins, A and C lose) + P(C wins, A and B lose) = (1/2)(2/3)(3/4) + (1/2)(1/3)(3/4) + (1/2)(2/3)(1/4) = 6/24 + 3/24 + 2/24 = 11/24.

records.hold_reason: The individual winning probabilities do not specify independence or the joint outcomes. Exactly-one probability is not determined by these marginals, and independence cannot be added as an unstated substantive condition.
